channel.title: CrimeTimeSnacks Blog
channel.description: True crime case updates, analysis, and the stories behind the headlines.

item.title: The Killing of JonBenét Ramsey: What the Record Shows
item.description: The 1996 death of six-year-old JonBenét Ramsey remains unsolved, but the case file contains specific, documented facts that cut through decades of rumors.

item.title: The Fingerprint That Changed the Courtroom
item.description: Before automated databases, one bloody print in 1892 changed criminal investigation forever. Here is how fingerprint evidence actually began.

item.title: What Reasonable Doubt Actually Means in a Courtroom
item.description: TV dramas make reasonable doubt look like a gut feeling. The actual jury instructions tell a very different story. Let's unpack it.

item.title: When the Case File Gets It Wrong
item.description: The Innocence Project has helped exonerate more than 200 people convicted of serious crimes. Here's what the record shows about how it happens.

item.title: How Familial DNA Searching Actually Works
item.description: It's not magic. It's probability, patience, and a whole lot of investigative follow-up. Let's unpack what the case file really shows.

item.title: What Actually Gets a Cold Case Reopened
item.description: It's not a tip line call or a true crime podcast. The decision to reopen a case comes down to something much more specific.

item.title: What You Saw and What Happened Are Not the Same Thing
item.description: Eyewitness testimony feels like the gold standard in court. The case file shows it's one of the most fragile kinds of evidence we have.

item.title: Why Solid Evidence Gets Thrown Out of Court
item.description: The evidence looked airtight. Then a judge tossed it. Here's what chain of custody actually means for a case.

item.title: How Forensic Genealogy Is Reopening Cases the System Had Written Off
item.description: A DNA sample that sat in an evidence freezer for decades can now build a family tree. Here's what the record shows.

item.title: The Documented Facts of the JonBenét Ramsey Case
item.description: The ransom note demanded a very specific dollar amount. Here is what the evidence actually shows about the 1996 killing of six-year-old JonBenét Ramsey.

item.title: Wilmington DMV: What the Record Shows
item.description: Corporal Grade One Matthew "Ty" Snook of the Delaware State Police was killed on December 23, 2025, at the DMV on Hessler Boulevard. Here is what the State Police investigation has put on the record.

item.title: The Watts Family Murders: What the Record Shows
item.description: Christopher Watts murdered his pregnant wife and two daughters in 2018. Here is what the timeline and evidence actually show about the case.

item.title: The Courtney Clenney Case: What the Evidence Shows
item.description: Courtney Clenney claimed she threw a knife from ten feet away, but the autopsy told a different story. Here is what the case file actually reveals.

item.title: The 2022 University of Idaho Student Murders
item.description: The documented facts behind the 2022 murders of four University of Idaho students and the digital trail that led to Bryan Christopher Kohberger.

item.title: The Case File: Erik and Lyle Menendez
item.description: The documented facts behind the 1989 Beverly Hills murders, the deadlocked juries, and the recent resentencing of Erik and Lyle Menendez.

item.title: The Delphi Murders: What the Record Shows
item.description: A look at the documented timeline, the evidence recovered from Libby German's phone, and the tip that led to Richard Allen's 2022 arrest.

item.title: Investigative Genetic Genealogy
item.description: Here is what the record actually shows about how law enforcement uses public DNA databases to solve decades-old cold cases.
